rationale: Recorded the store property that the measured gap depends on, so the aborted-append account's consequence is not read as a property of the log store contract. The in-memory store writes entries by index into a map and only tracks the lowest and highest index it has seen, so it accepts an entry whose predecessors are missing and then reports that entry as its last index; that is why the accepted append in the probe left index 4 sitting above a hole. A store that enforced contiguity would instead reject or handle that write, which makes the persistence of the gap an assumption of the measurement rather than a guarantee of the interface.

knowledge.statement: The in-memory log store accepts non-contiguous writes: StoreLogs stores each entry by its index into a map, initialises its low index from the first entry it ever sees and raises its high index whenever a larger index arrives, without checking that the entries continue the range it already holds. An entry stored above a missing range therefore persists and is reported by LastIndex, which is what let the aborted-append probe end with index 4 in a store that no longer held indices 2 and 3. The LogStore interface does not require that tolerance, so a store that validates contiguity would reject or handle that write differently.
knowledge.conditions: In-memory log store used by the probe and by tests; the aborted append that stores an entry beyond the deleted suffix is what leaves the hole. Other LogStore implementations are not covered by this behavior.
